done_when: When core.hooksPath is husky's folder, forge sync puts one line that runs Forge's pre-commit and pre-push checks (through .forge/hooks.sh) into the repo's committed .husky/pre-commit and .husky/pre-push, keeping their existing lines, and writes no shims into the folder husky rebuilds; the checks still run after npm install rebuilds that folder, in every worktree and a fresh clone; doctor reports the hooks installed in that setup; repos without husky keep today's shims; command tests cover a new husky repo and a husky repo adopted on an earlier release (including its earlier .pre-forge shims cleaned up)

findings.body: This previously reported gap remains open for both hooks. The generated line sources hooks.sh before calling forge_husky, so the child at this line inherits the PATH modifications at src/forge/sync.py:78–81. Husky deliberately puts node_modules/.bin first (tests/fixtures/husky-v9.1.7/husky:16), but Forge's launcher moves global executable directories ahead of it. An existing `eslint .` hook consequently runs global ESLint instead of the repository's pinned executable when both exist. The isolation ruling addresses exit/exec and stdin, but does not require changing the user commands' environment. Preserve the incoming PATH for the user script and apply the launcher PATH only to Forge.
findings.title: Preserve Husky's PATH when running existing user hooks

findings.body: This previously reported gap remains open. An absolute core.hooksPath pointing to the original checkout's .husky/_ is accepted there, but Git shares that configuration with linked worktrees. The operational evidence beyond the absolute-path detection ruling is that upgrade creates another checkout at src/forge/upgrade.py:99 and runs sync there at line 146: this guard rejects the configured folder because it lies outside that checkout. Close's verification checkout (src/forge/close.py:362–364), merge-conflict inventory (src/forge/close.py:321–323), and oversized-fix inventory (src/forge/sync.py:369) encounter the same rejection. Handle this accepted configuration explicitly in these workflows while retaining protection against writes outside the checkout.
findings.title: Handle absolute Husky paths during worktree-based upgrade and close

why: In client repos that use husky, every npm install rebuilds husky's hooks folder (core.hooksPath .husky/_) and wipes Forge's pre-commit and pre-push shims, so doctor reports the git hooks missing in every worktree after install (reported by a client session on v1.2.7). Owner decision 2026-10-08: add Forge to husky's own committed hooks
